title: Feelings & opinions
goal: Say how you feel, give and ask for opinions, agree and disagree, and link ideas with because, but and so.
intro:
This unit lets you go beyond facts: happy, tired, worried, bored; 'I think…', 'I don't think so', 'you're absolutely right'.

You'll notice two ways of expressing feelings: some are adjectives (**मैं ख़ुश हूँ** 'I'm happy'), while others are nouns that 'come to' you (**मुझे ग़ुस्सा आ रहा है** 'I'm getting angry'). And the most common way to give an opinion uses our old friend लगना: **मुझे लगता है कि…** 'it seems to me that…'.

grammar.title: Two ways to express feelings
grammar.body:
**1. Adjective + होना** — 'I am happy': मैं **ख़ुश** हूँ, वह **उदास** है, हम **परेशान** हैं. Most of these adjectives are invariable; थका, अकेला agree (मैं थकी हूँ, f).

Tiredness and boredom are often expressed as something that has happened: **मैं थक गया हूँ** 'I've got tired', **मैं बोर हो रहा हूँ** 'I'm getting bored'.

**2. Dative + noun + verb** — the feeling 'comes to' or 'strikes' you:

मुझे **ग़ुस्सा आता है** 'I get angry' · मुझे **शर्म आती है** 'I feel shy' · मुझे **मज़ा आया** 'I enjoyed it'
मुझे **डर लगता है** 'I'm afraid' · मुझे **अच्छा लगा** 'I liked it'
मुझे **चिंता है** 'I'm worried' · मुझे **उम्मीद है** 'I hope'

The verb agrees with the feeling-noun: ग़ुस्सा (m) **आया**, शर्म (f) **आई**. The cause takes **से** (कुत्तों से डर) or **पर** for anger (मुझे उस पर ग़ुस्सा आया 'I got angry at him').

examples.native: मुझे अँधेरे से डर लगता है।

grammar.title: Giving opinions: मुझे लगता है कि…
grammar.body:
The most natural way to say 'I think (that)…' is **मुझे लगता है कि…** — literally 'it seems to me that…'. Others:

**मेरे ख़याल से…** 'in my view…' · **मेरी राय में…** 'in my opinion…' (more formal)
**मैं सोचता/सोचती हूँ कि…** — correct, but sounds more like 'I'm thinking / I reckon' than a quick opinion.

Ask: **आपको क्या लगता है?** 'what do you think?'
Agree: **मैं आपसे सहमत हूँ** · **आप सही कह रहे हैं** · **बिल्कुल!** · **हाँ, सच में**
Disagree politely: **मुझे ऐसा नहीं लगता** 'I don't think so' · **मैं सहमत नहीं हूँ** · **शायद, लेकिन…** 'maybe, but…'

The word **कि** 'that' joins the opinion to the main clause, and unlike English it is almost never left out.

examples.native: मुझे लगता है कि वह आज नहीं आएगा।
examples.roman: mujhe lagtā hai ki vah āj nahīṃ āyegā.

examples.en: I think this film is good.

examples.native: आपको क्या लगता है, यह सही है?
examples.roman: āpko kyā lagtā hai, yah sahī hai?
examples.en: What do you think — is this right?

examples.native: मैं सोच रही हूँ कि घर चलूँ।
examples.roman: maiṃ soch rahī hūṃ ki ghar chalūṃ.

examples.native: आप बिल्कुल सही कह रहे हैं।
examples.roman: āp bilkul sahī kah rahe haiṃ.

grammar.title: Linking ideas: क्योंकि, लेकिन, इसलिए, तो
grammar.body:
**और** 'and' · **या** 'or' · **लेकिन / पर / मगर** 'but' · **क्योंकि** 'because' · **इसलिए** 'so, that's why' · **तो** 'so, then'

They work much like English and come at the start of their clause:

मैं थका हूँ, **क्योंकि** मैंने बहुत काम किया।
मैं थका हूँ, **इसलिए** मैं घर जा रहा हूँ।

**तो** is extremely common in speech as 'so / well then', and also as an emphasis particle after a word: मैं **तो** ठीक हूँ 'I'm fine (at least)'. **पर** 'but' is the most common in conversation; **लेकिन** is neutral; **मगर** is a bit literary.

examples.native: खाना अच्छा था, लेकिन बहुत तीखा।
examples.roman: khānā achchhā thā, lekin bahut tīkhā.
examples.en: The food was good, but very spicy.

examples.native: मैं ख़ुश हूँ क्योंकि आज छुट्टी है।
examples.roman: maiṃ xush hūṃ kyoṃki āj chhuṭṭī hai.
examples.en: I'm happy because it's a holiday today.

examples.native: बारिश हो रही थी, इसलिए हम घर पर रहे।
examples.roman: bārish ho rahī thī, isliye ham ghar par rahe.
examples.en: It was raining, so we stayed at home.
So, what shall we do today?

dialogue.title: After the film
dialogue.setting: Pooja and Arjun come out of a cinema and argue about the new Bollywood film. They're friends and use तुम.

lines.speaker: Pooja
lines.en: So? How did you like the film?

lines.speaker: Arjun
lines.native: सच कहूँ? मैं बहुत बोर हो गया।
lines.roman: sach kahūṃ? maiṃ bahut bor ho gayā.

lines.speaker: Pooja
lines.native: क्या? मुझे तो बहुत मज़ा आया! गाने कितने अच्छे थे!
lines.roman: kyā? mujhe to bahut mazā āyā! gāne kitne achchhe the!
lines.en: What? I had a great time! The songs were so good!

lines.speaker: Arjun
lines.native: गाने ठीक थे, लेकिन कहानी बहुत लंबी थी।
lines.roman: gāne ṭhīk the, lekin kahānī bahut lambī thī.
lines.en: The songs were OK, but the story was way too long.

lines.speaker: Pooja
lines.native: मुझे ऐसा नहीं लगता। मेरे ख़याल से कहानी बहुत प्यारी थी।
lines.roman: mujhe aisā nahīṃ lagtā. mere xayāl se kahānī bahut pyārī thī.
lines.en: I don't think so. I thought the story was really sweet.

lines.speaker: Arjun
lines.native: हीरो की एक्टिंग अच्छी थी, यह मैं मानता हूँ।
lines.roman: hīro kī ekṭiṅg achchhī thī, yah maiṃ māntā hūṃ.
lines.en: The hero's acting was good, I'll admit that.

lines.speaker: Pooja
lines.native: बिल्कुल! और आख़िर में मैं रो रही थी, क्योंकि वह बहुत अकेला था।
lines.roman: bilkul! aur āxir meṃ maiṃ ro rahī thī, kyoṃki vah bahut akelā thā.
lines.en: Absolutely! And at the end I was crying, because he was so lonely.

lines.speaker: Arjun
lines.native: सच में? तुम रो रही थीं? मुझे लगा कि तुम सो रही हो!
lines.roman: sach meṃ? tum ro rahī thīṃ? mujhe lagā ki tum so rahī ho!
lines.en: Really? You were crying? I thought you were asleep!

lines.speaker: Pooja
lines.native: बहुत मज़ाक़िया हो तुम! चलो, अब मुझे भूख लगी है, इसलिए खाना तुम खिलाओगे।
lines.roman: bahut mazāqiyā ho tum! chalo, ab mujhe bhūkh lagī hai, isliye khānā tum khilāoge.
lines.en: Very funny! Come on, now I'm hungry, so you're buying dinner.

culture: Indians often express disagreement indirectly — 'शायद…', 'देखते हैं' ('we'll see') or a vague 'हाँ, हाँ' can politely mean 'no'. The famous Indian **head wobble** (a side-to-side tilt) usually means 'yes', 'OK' or 'I'm listening', not 'no'. Bollywood is a national conversation topic: films, songs and actors are safe, fun subjects with almost anyone. Strong emotions are expressed openly within families, but public displays of affection between couples are still frowned upon in many places.
